institutions.name: Post Office Limited
institutions.role: Institutional prosecutor and Horizon user discussed in CCRC case review

institutions.name: Criminal Cases Review Commission
institutions.role: Independent criminal conviction review and referrals to appellate courts

institutions.name: UK Parliament

cases.title: Dutch childcare benefits: discrimination in nationality-based administrative risk processing

institutions.name: Dutch Tax Administration / Benefits Office
institutions.role: Public administrator whose data-processing practices were investigated

institutions.name: Tweede Kamer parliamentary inquiry committee
institutions.role: Parliamentary examiner of childcare-benefit administration and rule-of-law failures

institutions.name: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens
institutions.role: Independent Dutch personal-data supervisory and enforcement authority

findings.statement: The CCRC reported material risk that Horizon bugs created apparent accounting shortfalls and that the Post Office failed to disclose the full picture of system reliability.
The Horizon System Offences Act 2024 quashed only convictions meeting statutory requirements in England and Wales or Northern Ireland, excluding certain convictions already considered on appeal.
The statutory Horizon Inquiry published Volume 1 of its final report on human impact and redress; publication is evidence of an inquiry finding and response, not independently proven prevention.
The parliamentary inquiry concluded that fundamental rule-of-law principles had been violated and criticized the rigid all-or-nothing handling of childcare benefit cases across the public system.
The Dutch data authority imposed a 2.75 million euro fine for discriminatory and unlawful nationality data processing in childcare benefit administration, including use in automated risk designation.

interventions.scope_note: The CCRC description establishes an independent channel for reviewing convictions and referring eligible cases; this is an observation date, not the date the review body first existed.
Automatic relief applies only where the statutory conditions for relevant offences, time, prosecuting authority, work and Horizon use are met; this Act does not extend to Scotland.
Volume 1 published a record and recommendations concerning human impact and redress, but this milestone did not examine the full original report or verify implementation results.
A national parliamentary inquiry made institutional findings about rule-of-law and administrative failures; such findings do not alone establish a claimant's individualized restitution.
The privacy authority imposed a fine for unlawful and discriminatory data processing; an administrative fine is distinct from direct monetary compensation paid to affected families.

comparisons.analysis: An independent criminal-conviction reviewer and a privacy supervisory authority provide different checks on machine-influenced decisions. Their powers, evidentiary standards and remedies are not interchangeable, but each exposes the need for accessible challenge and source transparency.

The UK statute alters qualifying conviction status, whereas the Dutch administrative fine sanctions public-sector data misconduct and does not itself reimburse individual claimants. Neither statutory eligibility counts nor compensation completion rates were independently reconciled.

An independent statutory inquiry and a parliamentary investigative commission can both document institutional breakdown, but they differ in authority, procedures and institutional incentives. Their published findings do not by themselves demonstrate that later safeguards prevented recurrence.

evidence_gaps.record_needed: Official case-level conviction and quashing registers with procedural eligibility and dates
evidence_gaps.question: Which individual convictions were covered by the 2024 Act as distinct from prior appellate review?

evidence_gaps.record_needed: Official redress and compensation disbursement reconciliation by cohort and status
evidence_gaps.question: How completely and promptly did the remediation process reach affected people, beyond announcement and legal eligibility?

evidence_gaps.record_needed: Anonymised risk-classification, individual administrative decision and appeal records with lawful access controls
evidence_gaps.question: How did nationality risk flags affect specific claimant decisions and the ability to contest them?

evidence_gaps.record_needed: Official aggregate restitution decisions and subsequent judicial or administrative review of the DPA sanction
evidence_gaps.question: What remedies actually reached affected families and what was the eventual procedural status of the regulatory fine?
